Complete Schedule 29 with the Alberta AT1 return.
File within the statutory deadline.

programmes.amount_note: Up to CAD 10,000 (typically covering up to 75% of eligible costs) to buy services from an approved service provider for early technical or market validation.
programmes.deadline_note: Continuous intake while the annual budget lasts; Alberta Innovates closes intake when the allocation is committed.

procedure_steps.detail: Create an account in the Alberta Innovates system.
Obtain a quote from an eligible service provider.
Submit the application with the quote and project description.
Approval, then reimbursement on completion.

eligibility.other_note: Alberta-incorporated SMEs with fewer than 50 FTEs; work must be done by an approved third-party service provider.

programmes.amount_note: Up to CAD 150,000 to demonstrate a near-market technology with a first customer in a real operating environment; matching contribution required.
programmes.deadline_note: Registration for the most recent intake closed on 29 May 2026 at 16:00.
programmes.reopen_note: Alberta Innovates runs the Product Demonstration Program as recurring intakes with a registration deadline followed by a full application deadline. Watch albertainnovates.ca/funding for the next intake announcement.

procedure_steps.detail: Register by the published registration deadline.
Secure a demonstration host or first customer with a letter of support.
Submit the full application with matched funding.
Review and funding agreement.

documents_required.doc: Letter of support from the demonstration host

eligibility.other_note: Alberta-based technology companies with a validated prototype ready for field demonstration. An active Micro Voucher or prior Alberta Innovates relationship is common but not always required.

programmes.source_snippet: Product Demonstration Program provides up to $150000 to Alberta tech companies. Registration closed: May 29, 2026 4:00 pm.

programmes.amount_note: Repayable contributions of up to CAD 10 million per project, normally covering up to 50% of eligible costs, to commercialise or adopt agri-innovations.
programmes.deadline_note: Continuous intake under the Sustainable Canadian Agricultural Partnership until funds are fully committed.

procedure_steps.detail: Submit a project summary form.
AAFC screens and invites a full application.
Full application with detailed budget and repayment plan.
Contribution agreement.

eligibility.other_note: For-profit organisations, co-operatives and Indigenous groups in the agriculture, agri-food or agri-based products sector.

programmes.amount_note: Up to CAD 300,000 over three years for industry-academia teams solving problems in natural resources and applied sciences; matched funding is required.
programmes.deadline_note: Ignite runs competitive intakes with fixed closing dates rather than continuous intake; check the Innovate BC programme page for the currently open round.
programmes.reopen_note: Historically run as roughly annual rounds with applications closing in the winter. Innovate BC announces new intakes on innovatebc.ca.

procedure_steps.detail: Form a team of at least one BC company and one BC research institution.
Submit the application by the round deadline.
Expert panel review.
Funding agreement and milestone reporting.

eligibility.other_note: Requires a BC-based company and a BC academic partner; project must have a clear path to market within three years.

programmes.amount_note: Funds BC technology companies to pilot and test solutions at designated testbed sites (such as ports and airports). Funding amount is scoped per pilot; no single published cap.
programmes.deadline_note: Rolling intake, stated by Innovate BC to remain open until at least March 2026, with programme funding expected to continue until March 2028; the intake process may be revised in spring or summer 2026.
programmes.reopen_note: Innovate BC has flagged that the intake process may be revised in Spring or Summer 2026 even though programme funding runs to March 2028.

procedure_steps.detail: Review the active testbed challenges.
Submit an application describing the solution and pilot plan.
Matching with a testbed host.
Pilot agreement and delivery.

eligibility.other_note: BC-based technology companies with a deployable solution suitable for a real-world testbed.

programmes.source_snippet: IM is currently accepting applications through a rolling intake process, which will remain open until at least March 2026.

programmes.name_local: BC Interactive Digital Media Tax Credit (IDMTC)
programmes.name_en: BC Interactive Digital Media Tax Credit (IDMTC)
programmes.funder: Government of British Columbia / Canada Revenue Agency
programmes.amount_note: Refundable credit of 25% (raised to 25% from 17.5% in recent budgets) of eligible BC labour costs for interactive digital media products such as video games. No per-company cap, but a minimum of CAD 100,000 of eligible salaries applies.
programmes.deadline_note: Registration with the BC Ministry of Finance is required, and the claim is filed with the corporate return within 18 months of the tax year end.

procedure_steps.detail: Register the company with the BC Ministry of Finance for IDMTC.
Track eligible BC labour costs.
File Schedule 429 with the T2 return.

eligibility.other_note: Corporation with a BC permanent establishment developing interactive digital media products; at least CAD 100,000 in eligible BC salaries in the year.

programmes.funder: Innovate BC (delivered through regional accelerator partners)
programmes.amount_note: Subsidised executive-in-residence coaching rather than cash. Participants pay a reduced monthly fee; Innovate BC covers the balance.
programmes.deadline_note: Rolling intake through regional delivery partners across BC.

procedure_steps.detail: Contact a regional VAP delivery partner.
Screening interview.
Enrolment and assignment of an executive-in-residence.
Milestone-based coaching.

eligibility.other_note: BC-based technology entrepreneurs; open to pre-incorporation founders in some partner locations.

programmes.name_en: BDC LIFT (digital, AI and equipment adoption advisory and financing)
programmes.amount_note: Preferential-rate consulting and financing to adopt AI, digital tools and smart equipment. No published fixed amount; BDC positions LIFT as the route for businesses that would previously have used CDAP.
programmes.deadline_note: Rolling intake; BDC directs former CDAP applicants here.

procedure_steps.detail: Contact BDC to scope the digital or AI adoption project.
Advisory engagement at preferential rates.
Optional financing for implementation.

eligibility.other_note: For-profit Canadian businesses; BDC assesses commercially.

programmes.source_snippet: BDC now recommends the LIFT program for businesses interested in digital transformation

programmes.name_en: BDC Start-up Financing / Small Business Loan
programmes.amount_note: Two distinct online products are advertised: Start-up Financing — 'Get up to $150,000 to grow your business'; Small Business Loan — 'Get up to $350,000 online quickly and easily'. Interest rates and terms are quoted individually; not published on the page.
programmes.deadline_note: Continuous — commercial lending, no calls or deadlines.

procedure_steps.detail: Check eligibility online.
Tell BDC about your financing needs.
Receive a tailored solution based on your financial profile.

documents_required.doc: Business financial statements / evidence of sales

eligibility.other_note: Business must be registered in Canada, have recorded sales, have good personal and business credit standing, all shareholders of legal age, and maintain a business bank account. BDC is a Crown corporation lending on commercial terms — this is debt, not a grant.

programmes.source_snippet: Start-up Financing: Get up to $150,000 to grow your business. ... Small Business Loan: Get up to $350,000 online quickly and easily. ... Your business has recorded sales.

programmes.name_local: Fonds de prêts pour l'entrepreneuriat des Noirs
programmes.funder: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED) with the Federation of African Canadian Economics (FACE)
programmes.amount_note: Loans from CAD 25,000 to CAD 250,000 to Black-owned businesses, delivered mainly through FACE and partner lenders; a micro-loan tier below CAD 25,000 has also been offered.
programmes.deadline_note: Rolling applications through FACE.

procedure_steps.detail: Apply on the FACE online platform.
Provide business plan and financials.
Credit assessment.
Loan agreement and disbursement.

eligibility.other_note: Majority Black-owned or Black-led Canadian businesses.

programmes.name_en: Canada Media Fund Experimental Stream / Innovation and Experimentation Program
programmes.amount_note: Funding for interactive digital media content and software applications, including video games, across concept, prototyping and production phases. Contribution ceilings are set per component in the annual program guidelines.
programmes.deadline_note: Program deadlines are published in the CMF annual program guidelines, typically with one or two intakes per component per year.

eligibility.other_note: Canadian-controlled companies; content must meet CMF Canadian content and ownership tests.

programmes.funder: Global Affairs Canada, Trade Commissioner Service
programmes.amount_note: Up to CAD 75,000 covering up to 75% of eligible costs of pursuing a single R&D collaboration agreement with a foreign partner.
programmes.deadline_note: Continuous intake within the federal fiscal year while funds last.

procedure_steps.detail: Identify a specific foreign R&D partner and target agreement.
Register on the CanExport portal and submit the application before travel or costs are incurred.
Sign the contribution agreement.
Claim eligible costs (travel, IP protection abroad, consultants, certification).

documents_required.doc: Description of the technology and its stage
Named foreign partner and target agreement

eligibility.other_note: Canadian SMEs, academic institutions and non-profit research centres seeking an international R&D partnership for a specific technology.

programmes.funder: Global Affairs Canada – Trade Commissioner Service
programmes.amount_note: 'Successful projects may receive up to $50,000 in funding for international business development activities.' The programme shares the cost of export-related activities; the exact applicant cost share is set in the 2026-27 Applicant's guide (not read here).
programmes.deadline_note: For markets other than the United States: 'Deadline: Extended to August 31, 2026 at 12:00 PM (ET)'. Applications for U.S.-targeted projects are no longer accepted for this intake because the $3.1 million allocated to U.S. projects is fully allocated. Applications are assessed on a rolling competitive basis; the programme reopens with a new annual intake.

procedure_steps.detail: Use the 'Find out if you qualify' checklist to confirm the programme fits your business and export plans.
Read the 2026-27 Applicant's guide (eligible activities and expenses, assessment criteria).
Create a profile in the CanExport SMEs portal and submit the application.
Await assessment: up to 60 business days for non-U.S. markets, up to 90 business days for U.S. projects.

documents_required.doc: Completed online application form (see sample application form)
Export/market development plan and budget for the target market

documents_required.note: Detailed list is in the Applicant's guide

eligibility.other_note: 'It is intended for companies with meaningful economic ties to Canada, the capacity to grow internationally, and a clear plan to export Canadian goods and services.' Precise size thresholds are set in the Applicant's guide 2026-27.

programmes.source_snippet: Successful projects may receive up to $50,000 in funding for international business development activities. Funding is limited, and applications are assessed on a rolling competitive basis. ... Deadline: Extended to August 31, 2026 at 12:00 PM (ET)

programmes.name_local: Programme canadien d'adoption du numérique - Développez vos activités commerciales grâce à la technologie
programmes.name_en: Canada Digital Adoption Program - Boost Your Business Technology
programmes.funder: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada / Business Development Bank of Canada (BDC)
programmes.amount_note: Grant of up to CAD 15,000 covering 90% of the cost of a digital adoption plan, plus an interest-free BDC loan of up to CAD 100,000 to implement it.
programmes.deadline_note: Closed to new applications on 19 February 2024. Only businesses that had a signed grant agreement with ISED before that date can complete their plan and access the associated 0% loan.
programmes.reopen_note: No successor grant announced. BDC now directs digital-transformation applicants to its LIFT programme of preferential-rate advisory services and financing. As of August 2026 the federal government has not published plans to relaunch CDAP.

procedure_steps.detail: Not applicable - closed to new applicants.

eligibility.other_note: Was open to for-profit Canadian incorporated businesses with 1-499 FTEs and at least CAD 500,000 annual revenue in one of the previous three tax years.

programmes.source_snippet: The Canada Digital Adoption Program (CDAP) is no longer accepting new applications for the Boost Your Business Technology stream

programmes.name_local: Creative BC - Interactive Digital Media funding
programmes.name_en: Creative BC Interactive Digital Media programs
programmes.amount_note: Sector-specific funding streams covering interactive digital media, domestic motion picture, book and magazine publishing and music (Amplify BC). Amounts are set per program in the annual guidelines.
programmes.deadline_note: Each industry stream has its own intake dates published on the Creative BC programs pages.

eligibility.other_note: Companies must be based and operating in British Columbia.

programmes.source_snippet: Creative BC funding programs drive the creation and export of domestic creative content.

programmes.amount_note: No fee and no equity taken by CDL itself, though mentors may invest personally. Free nine-month objectives-based programme.
programmes.deadline_note: Annual application cycle closing in the summer (typically June or July) for a programme starting in September
programmes.reopen_note: Runs annually across sites in Canada, the US and Europe with multiple science-based streams (Quantum, Climate, Health, Space, AI). Applications usually open in the spring.

eligibility.other_note: Massively scalable, science-based ventures. Open to companies worldwide, but founders must attend sessions at a CDL site.

programmes.amount_note: EDC guarantees a share of a loan made by the company's own bank (commonly up to 75% of the loan, and up to 100% for some foreign-asset transactions), unlocking additional working capital rather than paying cash to the company.
programmes.deadline_note: No deadlines; applied for through the company's commercial bank.

procedure_steps.detail: Discuss the working-capital need with your bank.
Bank applies to EDC for a guarantee on the incremental facility.
EDC underwrites and issues the guarantee.
Bank advances the increased facility.

eligibility.other_note: Canadian exporters or companies investing abroad; the applicant works through its existing lender.

programmes.name_local: Programme de démarrage pour entrepreneurs noirs
programmes.amount_note: Up to CAD 75,000 in co-loan financing (Futurpreneur plus BDC) mirroring the core programme, with mentorship and tailored resources.

procedure_steps.detail: Self-identify as a Black entrepreneur in the application.
Submit business plan and cash flow.
Mentor matching.
Loan approval and disbursement.

documents_required.doc: Proof of citizenship or permanent residency

eligibility.other_note: Black entrepreneurs aged 18-39 (age range has been widened in some intakes); business operating full-time 24 months or less.

programmes.name_local: Programme de démarrage de base Futurpreneur
programmes.amount_note: Co-loan of up to CAD 75,000: up to CAD 25,000 from Futurpreneur plus up to CAD 50,000 from BDC, bundled with up to two years of mandatory mentorship.
programmes.deadline_note: Rolling applications; no calls.

procedure_steps.detail: Check eligibility (age 18-39, business operating full-time for 24 months or less).
Complete the online application with a business plan and cash flow.
Interview and matching with a volunteer mentor.
Loan approval and disbursement; two-year mentorship begins.

documents_required.doc: Proof of Canadian citizenship or permanent residency

eligibility.other_note: Founders aged 18-39, Canadian citizens or permanent residents, business must be operating full time for 24 months or less and be majority owned by the applicant(s).

programmes.source_snippet: We offer young entrepreneurs up to $75,000 in startup loan financing and up to two years of mentorship.

programmes.name_local: Programme de démarrage pour entrepreneurs autochtones
programmes.amount_note: Up to CAD 75,000 in co-loan financing plus mentorship, with eligibility and structure mirroring the core programme.

procedure_steps.detail: Self-identify as First Nations, Inuit or Métis.
Submit application, business plan and cash flow.
Mentor matching.
Loan approval and disbursement.

documents_required.doc: Proof of citizenship or permanent residency

eligibility.other_note: Indigenous entrepreneurs; business operating full-time 24 months or less.

programmes.funder: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
programmes.amount_note: Phase 1 proof-of-feasibility contracts commonly up to CAD 150,000 for six months; Phase 2 prototype contracts commonly up to CAD 1 million for up to two years. This is procurement of R&D, so the company keeps the IP.
programmes.deadline_note: Individual challenges open and close on their own dates throughout the year; check the ISC challenge list for the currently open ones.

procedure_steps.detail: Browse open challenges on the ISC website.
Register in BuyandSell / CanadaBuys and submit a Phase 1 proposal by the challenge deadline.
If selected, deliver the Phase 1 feasibility study under contract.
Compete for a Phase 2 prototype contract.

documents_required.doc: Technical proposal responding to the challenge

eligibility.other_note: For-profit incorporated in Canada with 499 or fewer FTEs; solution must be at a defined technology readiness level range for the challenge.

programmes.funder: Government of Manitoba, Department of Economic Development, Investment, Trade and Natural Resources
programmes.amount_note: Matching grant of up to CAD 100,000 per project (50% of eligible costs) to help Manitoba SMEs develop and commercialise new products.
programmes.deadline_note: Manitoba runs IGP as periodic intakes; the programme has been oversubscribed and intake has been paused between rounds.
programmes.reopen_note: Manitoba has historically reopened IGP intake at the start of the provincial fiscal year (April). Confirm the current intake status with Manitoba Economic Development before preparing an application.

procedure_steps.detail: Confirm the intake is open with the department.
Submit the application form with project plan and budget.
Assessment.
Grant agreement and milestone claims.

eligibility.other_note: Manitoba-based SMEs commercialising a new product or process; must be incorporated in Manitoba.

procedure_steps.detail: Find an academic partner (professor and graduate student or postdoc) at a Canadian university.
Co-develop the research proposal with the academic supervisor.
Submit through the Mitacs online system with the company's cash contribution committed.
Peer review; on approval the intern begins and Mitacs matches the funds.

documents_required.doc: Company profile and financial commitment letter

eligibility.other_note: Open to Canadian-incorporated companies of any size partnering with a Canadian postsecondary institution; the money is paid to the university to fund the intern, not to the company.

programmes.deadline_note: Elevate runs a limited number of national calls each year with fixed submission dates, unlike the rolling Accelerate programme.

procedure_steps.detail: Identify a postdoctoral fellow and academic supervisor.
Build the two-year R&D plan with the partner organisation.
Submit by the published call deadline.
Peer review and award.

eligibility.other_note: Partner organisations must be Canadian; the fellow must hold a PhD.

programmes.funder: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada, delivered via NRC, NSERC and the Regional Development Agencies
programmes.amount_note: CAD 360 million strategy covering research, talent and commercialisation. Company-facing funding flows mainly through the NRC Quantum Challenge programmes, NSERC Alliance grants and Regional Development Agency programmes.
programmes.deadline_note: Individual delivery programmes run their own intakes; the strategy itself is not a single application window.

eligibility.other_note: Canadian-incorporated companies; most instruments require collaboration with a Canadian research organisation.

programmes.name_local: New Brunswick Innovation Foundation (NBIF) Startup Investment
programmes.name_en: New Brunswick Innovation Foundation (NBIF) Startup Investment
programmes.amount_note: NBIF invests in New Brunswick startups, historically up to about CAD 500,000 per company across rounds, always alongside private co-investors, plus separate research and talent grants.
programmes.deadline_note: Rolling; NBIF also runs the annual Breakthru startup competition with a larger prize pool on a roughly biennial or annual cycle.
programmes.reopen_note: NBIF's Breakthru competition (prizes historically worth over CAD 1 million in cash and services) runs periodically; check nbif.ca for the next edition.

procedure_steps.detail: Submit the company through the NBIF investment enquiry form.
Screening and pitch.
Due diligence alongside a private lead investor.
Investment agreement.

eligibility.other_note: Startups based in or relocating to New Brunswick, with private co-investment.

programmes.name_local: Opportunities New Brunswick early-stage and venture support
programmes.name_en: Opportunities New Brunswick early-stage and venture support
programmes.amount_note: ONB provides payroll rebates, term loans and equity-style support to New Brunswick companies; amounts are negotiated case by case with no published grant ceiling for startups.
programmes.deadline_note: Rolling engagement through an ONB business development executive.

procedure_steps.detail: Contact an ONB business development executive.
Present the growth or R&D project with job creation numbers.
Negotiate the support package.
Agreement with performance conditions.

eligibility.other_note: New Brunswick-based companies; support is generally tied to job creation and payroll in the province.

programmes.name_local: NGen - Fabrication de prochaine génération Canada
programmes.name_en: NGen (Next Generation Manufacturing Canada) project funding
programmes.funder: Next Generation Manufacturing Canada (NGen), a Global Innovation Cluster
programmes.amount_note: Cost-shared contributions to collaborative advanced-manufacturing projects, typically covering up to about one third of eligible project costs. Amounts vary by call; NGen has run calls from roughly CAD 250,000 to several million per project.
programmes.deadline_note: NGen funds through periodic themed calls for proposals rather than continuous intake. Check the NGen funding page for the currently open call.
programmes.reopen_note: NGen is one of Canada's Global Innovation Clusters with funding committed under the cluster mandate; new calls are announced on ngen.ca and to members. Membership is free and is the way to be notified of new calls.

procedure_steps.detail: Become an NGen member (free).
Form a consortium of at least two companies, one of which must be an SME.
Submit an expression of interest to the open call.
Full proposal, review and contribution agreement.

documents_required.doc: Consortium agreement or letters of intent

eligibility.other_note: Projects must be industry-led and collaborative, involve advanced manufacturing in Canada, and demonstrate commercialisation potential.

programmes.name_local: Programme d'aide à la recherche industrielle du CNRC (PARI CNRC)
programmes.name_en: NRC Industrial Research Assistance Program (NRC IRAP) – financial support for technology innovation
programmes.funder: National Research Council Canada (NRC), Industrial Research Assistance Program
programmes.amount_note: No funding amounts, ceilings or cost-share percentages are published on the official NRC IRAP financial support page. Contributions are negotiated project by project with an Industrial Technology Advisor. Do not assume a published maximum.
programmes.deadline_note: No application deadlines are published; intake is continuous and starts by contacting NRC IRAP (1-877-994-4727).

procedure_steps.detail: Check the minimum requirements, then contact NRC IRAP at 1-877-994-4727.
A client engagement advisor reviews your business information and goals.

An Industrial Technology Advisor may assess innovation potential and business readiness and, if appropriate, invite a proposal. 'Working with an advisor or being invited to submit a proposal does not guarantee funding.'

documents_required.doc: Company and project information provided to the client engagement advisor
Project proposal (only if invited by an Industrial Technology Advisor)

eligibility.other_note: 'To work with NRC IRAP, your business must: be incorporated, for-profit, and operating in Canada' and employ up to 500 full-time-equivalent people. Unlimited/limited liability corporations (ULCs, LLCs), sole proprietorships, partnerships and cooperatives are not supported. Day-to-day operating costs, non-technical activities and work outside Canada are not funded.

programmes.source_snippet: To work with NRC IRAP, your business must: be incorporated, for-profit, and operating in Canada ... employ up to 500 people (full-time equivalent) ... Working with an advisor or being invited to submit a proposal does not guarantee funding.

programmes.name_local: PARI CNRC - Soutien aux technologies propres
programmes.name_en: NRC IRAP Support for Clean Technology (successor to SDTC funding)
programmes.funder: National Research Council of Canada, Industrial Research Assistance Program (NRC IRAP)
programmes.amount_note: No published ceiling. NRC IRAP funds staff and materials from proof of concept through to larger-scale multi-year demonstration projects, and can provide upfront funding where specific needs exist. This stream absorbed the funding role of the wound-down Sustainable Development Technology Canada (SDTC).
programmes.deadline_note: Rolling; access is via an NRC IRAP industrial technology advisor or the contact centre on 1-877-994-4727. No competitive call windows.

procedure_steps.detail: Confirm you meet the cleantech eligibility criteria (validated proof of concept, quantifiable environmental impact, commercialisation path).
Call 1-877-994-4727 or contact your existing industrial technology advisor.
Scope the project with the ITA and submit a proposal.
Contribution agreement and milestone-based claims.

documents_required.doc: Evidence of validated proof of concept
Quantified environmental impact plan (e.g. GHG reduction, air/soil/water quality)

eligibility.other_note: For-profit incorporated in Canada, max 500 FTE in Canada, paid full-time employees other than founders covering both technical and business roles.

programmes.source_snippet: Funding to jump-start promising clean technologies from proof of concept through to larger-scale, multi-year projects that create long-term environmental benefits

programmes.name_local: PARI CNRC - Aide financière à l'innovation technologique
programmes.name_en: NRC IRAP Financial Support for Technology Innovation
programmes.funder: National Research Council of Canada, Industrial Research Assistance Program (NRC IRAP)
programmes.amount_note: Non-repayable contributions covering up to 75% of eligible salary and up to 50% of eligible contractor costs; historically capped around CAD 10 million per firm per year for the largest projects. There is no published fixed grant amount - the advisor scopes the contribution to the project.
programmes.deadline_note: No calls or deadlines. Entry is by phoning the NRC IRAP contact centre (1-877-994-4727); funding follows an advisor relationship.

procedure_steps.detail: A senior executive of the business calls 1-877-994-4727; the bilingual contact centre screens minimum requirements.
Meet a client engagement advisor (CEA) who reviews the business and may refer you onward.
Work with an industrial technology advisor (ITA) who assesses technical, financial and management capacity.
If invited, submit a project proposal; contribution agreement signed and costs claimed monthly in arrears.

documents_required.doc: Resumes or profiles of management and technical team

eligibility.other_note: Must be incorporated and for-profit. NRC IRAP does not support unlimited/limited liability corporations (ULCs or LLCs), sole proprietorships, partnerships or cooperatives.

programmes.source_snippet: To work with NRC IRAP, your business must: be incorporated, for-profit, and operating in Canada; employ up to 500 people (full-time equivalent)

programmes.amount_note: Rebate of up to 25% of eligible innovation project costs, to a maximum of CAD 3.5 million, paid after the project is completed and verified.
programmes.deadline_note: Continuous intake; the rebate is paid in arrears against verified spend.

procedure_steps.detail: Discuss the project with Invest Nova Scotia.
Submit an application before incurring costs.
Approval and rebate agreement.
Complete the project, then claim the rebate against audited costs.

documents_required.doc: Evidence of ability to finance the full project

eligibility.other_note: Nova Scotia businesses making a minimum eligible innovation investment (historically CAD 500,000); the company must fund the project up front.

programmes.name_local: Invest Nova Scotia early stage commercialisation support (formerly Innovacorp)
programmes.name_en: Invest Nova Scotia early stage commercialisation support (formerly Innovacorp)
programmes.amount_note: Invest Nova Scotia (which absorbed Innovacorp and Nova Scotia Business Inc. in 2023) makes early-stage equity investments and provides incubation. procedure_steps.detail: Contact Invest Nova Scotia via the website.
Submit business plan and financials.
Due diligence.
Investment or incubation agreement.

eligibility.other_note: Nova Scotia-based knowledge economy startups.

programmes.funder: Ontario Ministry of Finance / Canada Revenue Agency
programmes.amount_note: 8% refundable tax credit on qualified SR&ED expenditures up to an annual expenditure limit of CAD 3 million, so a maximum of about CAD 240,000 per year. Claimed alongside the federal SR&ED claim.
programmes.deadline_note: Claimed on Schedule 566 with the corporate T2 return; same 18-month reporting deadline as federal SR&ED.

procedure_steps.detail: Prepare the federal SR&ED claim (Form T661).
Complete Ontario Schedule 566.
File with the T2 return.

eligibility.other_note: Corporation with a permanent establishment in Ontario carrying out SR&ED in Ontario; credit phases out based on taxable income and taxable capital.

programmes.amount_note: Subsidises the cost of hiring students, recent graduates or postdoctoral fellows into Ontario companies for defined R&D projects; internship values have historically been around CAD 10,000-15,000 per four-month term and fellowships up to about CAD 35,000.
programmes.deadline_note: Intake follows the Ontario fiscal year and pauses when the annual allocation is committed.
programmes.reopen_note: Refreshed annually with the Ontario budget cycle; watch oc-innovation.ca for the new fiscal year intake.

procedure_steps.detail: Register on AccessOCI.
Identify the intern or fellow and the project.
Submit application with company cash contribution.
Approval and placement.

eligibility.other_note: Ontario-based companies; intern must be enrolled at or recently graduated from an Ontario postsecondary institution.

programmes.amount_note: OCI contributes typically CAD 20,000 to CAD 100,000 towards a collaborative R&D project with an Ontario academic institution, matched at least 1:1 by the company in cash and in kind.
programmes.deadline_note: OCI operates VIP through periodic intakes; check the OCI programme page for the current intake as terms and ceilings have changed between rounds.
programmes.reopen_note: OCI is funded by Ontario's Ministry of Economic Development, Job Creation and Trade and refreshes its programme suite each fiscal year (April-March); new intakes are usually announced in the spring.

procedure_steps.detail: Identify an Ontario academic partner and principal investigator.
Register in the OCI AccessOCI portal.
Submit the joint application with matching-funds commitment.
Review and funding agreement.

eligibility.other_note: Ontario-based for-profit company collaborating with an Ontario publicly funded postsecondary institution or research hospital.

programmes.funder: Government of Ontario, Ministry of Economic Development, Job Creation and Trade
programmes.amount_note: Part of a CAD 50 million fund. Supports up to 75% of eligible project costs for smaller projects and a lower share for larger ones; grants for projects under CAD 10 million and loans above that.
programmes.deadline_note: Continuous intake with no fixed deadline; projects must be completed within 24 months of the start date.

procedure_steps.detail: Register on Transfer Payment Ontario (TPON).
Consult an Ontario regional advisor before applying.
Submit the application through TPON.
Assessment and funding agreement.

eligibility.other_note: Ontario businesses diversifying away from US markets to serve interprovincial and other export customers. Excludes refinancing of existing operations, electricity projects, waste management/primary recycling and hospitality (hotels and restaurants).

programmes.amount_note: Co-investment of up to 50% of eligible project costs in industry-led consortium projects across plant-protein ingredient processing, food innovation and agri-tech. No fixed per-project cap published.
programmes.deadline_note: Continuous project intake; the cluster also runs occasional themed calls.

procedure_steps.detail: Become a Protein Industries Canada member.
Form a consortium of at least two Canadian companies.
Submit a project concept, then a full application.
Due diligence and co-investment agreement.

eligibility.other_note: Industry-led consortia; benefits must accrue to the Canadian plant-protein and agri-food value chain.

programmes.name_local: Crédit d'impôt pour le développement des affaires électroniques (CDAE)
programmes.name_en: Crédit d'impôt pour le développement des affaires électroniques (CDAE)
programmes.amount_note: Payroll-based credit for IT companies, worth up to CAD 25,000 per eligible employee per year (a refundable portion plus a non-refundable portion). Rates were reduced and a non-refundable component introduced in recent Quebec budgets.
programmes.deadline_note: An eligibility certificate must be obtained from Investissement Québec for each taxation year, generally applied for within 15 months of the corporation's filing deadline.

procedure_steps.detail: Apply to Investissement Québec for the annual corporation eligibility certificate.
Obtain employee eligibility certificates.
Claim the credit on the CO-17 return.

documents_required.doc: Description of activities under eligible NAICS codes

eligibility.other_note: Requires a minimum proportion of revenue from eligible IT activities and a minimum number of full-time eligible employees (historically six).

programmes.name_local: Crédit d'impôt pour la recherche, l'innovation et la précommercialisation (CRIC)
programmes.name_en: Crédit d'impôt pour la recherche, l'innovation et la commercialisation (CRIC)
programmes.amount_note: Quebec's consolidated R&D and pre-commercialisation tax credit, which replaced several earlier R&D credits. The enhanced refundable rate is 30% on the first tranche of eligible expenditure with a 20% rate above it. Exact tranche thresholds are set in the Taxation Act - confirm with Revenu Québec for your tax year.
programmes.deadline_note: Claimed with the Quebec corporate income tax return; the filing deadline for the credit is 12 months after the income tax return due date.

procedure_steps.detail: Identify eligible R&D and pre-commercialisation expenditures.
Complete the CRIC form with the CO-17 corporate return.
Respond to any Revenu Québec review.

eligibility.other_note: Corporation with an establishment in Quebec carrying out eligible R&D or pre-commercialisation activity in Quebec. Replaced the former CDAE-adjacent R&D salary credits; confirm transitional rules for your fiscal year.

programmes.amount_note: Equity or quasi-equity co-investment of roughly CAD 250,000 to CAD 1.5 million in innovative Quebec SMEs, always alongside a qualified private lead investor who invests at least as much.
programmes.deadline_note: Rolling; Investissement Québec follows a private lead investor's round.

procedure_steps.detail: Secure a qualified private lead investor.
Contact Investissement Québec with the term sheet and business plan.
Due diligence.
Co-investment on the same terms as the lead.

eligibility.other_note: Innovative SMEs with a head office and majority of activities in Quebec.

programmes.name_en: Programme Innovation (volets Soutien aux projets d'innovation et Appui à la commercialisation)
programmes.funder: Ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie du Québec / Investissement Québec
programmes.amount_note: Non-repayable contributions generally covering up to 40% of eligible costs, commonly up to about CAD 350,000 per project for innovation projects and lower ceilings for commercialisation support. Rates are higher for some regions and for young firms.
programmes.deadline_note: Continuous intake while the programme envelope lasts; the MEIE republishes the normes each fiscal year.

procedure_steps.detail: Contact the regional MEIE office or Investissement Québec.
Submit the application with a technical and financial project description.
Analysis and offer letter.
Claims submitted against milestones.

eligibility.other_note: For-profit companies established in Quebec; project must involve innovation from development through to commercialisation.

programmes.funder: Scale AI (Canada's AI-Powered Supply Chains Global Innovation Cluster)
programmes.amount_note: Funding for AI startups and SMEs delivered through accredited accelerator and incubator partners. Scale AI does not publish a single fixed grant amount for this stream; support is scoped per cohort and partner.
programmes.deadline_note: Delivered through partner accelerators, each with its own cohort dates.

procedure_steps.detail: Review the list of Scale AI accredited acceleration partners.
Apply to a partner programme that fits your stage and sector.
Partner selects the cohort; Scale AI funding flows through the partner.

eligibility.other_note: Canadian AI startups and SMEs; supply chain and AI adoption focus.

programmes.source_snippet: Scale AI's Acceleration program puts millions in funding on the table to help finance the growth of AI startups and SMEs

programmes.funder: Scale AI (Canada's AI-Powered Supply Chains Global Innovation Cluster)
programmes.amount_note: Cost-shared contributions to collaborative AI adoption and commercialisation projects, generally covering up to 40% of eligible costs (up to 50% for projects executed in Quebec). Projects typically start around CAD 750,000 in total eligible costs.
programmes.deadline_note: Continuous intake with periodic evaluation committees.

procedure_steps.detail: Assemble a consortium (at least one technology provider and one AI user).
Submit a project outline to Scale AI.
Full application including budget and expected supply-chain impact.
Investment committee decision and contribution agreement.

eligibility.other_note: Consortium projects with Canadian-based execution; SMEs can participate as technology suppliers.

programmes.source_snippet: Scale AI funding: up to 40% of eligible project costs, 50% in Quebec

programmes.name_en: Sustainable Development Technology Canada - SD Tech Fund / Startup and Scale-up streams
programmes.amount_note: Historically the Startup stream gave up to about CAD 1 million and the Scale-up stream up to about CAD 5 million (typically up to 33-40% of project costs). No new SDTC agreements are being signed.
programmes.deadline_note: SDTC stopped accepting new applications in 2024 following the Auditor General's review; the organisation was wound down and its programmes transferred to the National Research Council.
programmes.reopen_note: Not reopening under the SDTC name. Cleantech funding was transferred to NRC IRAP, which began accepting new clean technology applications in fiscal 2025-26 under 'NRC IRAP support for clean technology' (https://nrc.canada.ca/en/support-technology-innovation/nrc-irap-support-clean-technology). Existing SDTC contribution agreements continue to be administered by NRC.

procedure_steps.detail: Not applicable - closed. Cleantech applicants should approach NRC IRAP instead.

eligibility.other_note: Historically required Canadian incorporation, a pre-commercial technology with quantified environmental benefit and at least 40% Canadian ownership of the project consortium.

programmes.source_snippet: Ottawa shutting down SDTC and transferring its programs to the National Research Council

programmes.name_local: Sustainable Development Technology Canada / Canada Growth Fund cleantech support
programmes.name_en: SDTC cleantech funding (now delivered by the National Research Council)
programmes.funder: National Research Council of Canada (successor to Sustainable Development Technology Canada)
programmes.amount_note: SDTC historically contributed up to roughly one third of eligible project costs for cleantech demonstration projects, typically CAD 1-10 million. Following governance reviews the portfolio was transferred to the National Research Council.
programmes.deadline_note: SDTC ceased operating as an independent foundation after a 2023-2024 governance review; its funding activities were moved to the National Research Council of Canada.
programmes.reopen_note: Cleantech demonstration funding continues through the National Research Council and Canada Growth Fund rather than under the SDTC brand. Check nrc.canada.ca for current intake.

eligibility.other_note: Canadian-incorporated companies with a pre-commercial cleantech project.

programmes.name_local: Innovation Saskatchewan Innovation Challenge / Made in Saskatchewan Technology Program
programmes.name_en: Innovation Saskatchewan Innovation Challenge / Made in Saskatchewan Technology Program
programmes.amount_note: Challenge-based procurement and pilot funding for Saskatchewan technology companies; amounts vary by challenge and are published with each call.
programmes.deadline_note: Individual challenges are published with their own opening and closing dates; there is no continuous intake.
programmes.reopen_note: Innovation Saskatchewan posts new challenges on innovationsask.ca as public-sector partners identify problems; sign up for notifications rather than waiting for a fixed annual date.

procedure_steps.detail: Monitor the Innovation Saskatchewan programme page for open challenges.
Submit a proposal to the specific challenge.
Evaluation and pilot contract.

eligibility.other_note: Saskatchewan-based technology companies with a deployable solution.

programmes.amount_note: A 45% non-refundable tax credit to investors in eligible Saskatchewan startups, capped at CAD 140,000 of credit per investor per year, with an annual programme cap. The benefit reaches the startup indirectly, as cheaper equity.
programmes.deadline_note: Eligible Startup Business (ESB) applications are accepted on a rolling basis; tax credits are issued against the annual programme allocation until exhausted.

procedure_steps.detail: Apply to Innovation Saskatchewan for Eligible Startup Business status.
Once approved, raise equity from eligible investors.
Investors apply for the tax credit certificate.
Report on use of funds.

documents_required.doc: Proof of Saskatchewan incorporation and head office

eligibility.other_note: Startup must be Saskatchewan-headquartered, fewer than 50 employees, developing a novel technology product, and have raised less than a specified amount of prior capital.

programmes.name_local: Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) tax incentives / Encouragements fiscaux à la RS&DE
programmes.name_en: Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) tax incentives
programmes.amount_note: No fixed award. Two incentives: a deduction against income, and an investment tax credit (ITC). CRA's ITC policy states 'CCPCs may earn the SR&ED ITC at an enhanced rate of 35%' on qualified expenditures up to an expenditure limit (the policy page states a maximum threshold of $3 million; the limit has been the subject of announced federal increases which we did not verify on the CRA page), and 'The basic rate of SR&ED ITC is 15%'. Refundability: up to 100% of the unclaimed balance earned at the 35% enhanced rate for qualifying CCPCs, and 40% of the unclaimed balance at the basic rate.
programmes.deadline_note: Claimed with the corporate income tax return for the year: 'Claimants should submit their SR&ED claim with their income tax return for the year.' Statutory reporting deadlines apply (not verified on this page).

procedure_steps.detail: Determine that your work meets the SR&ED definition (scientific or technological uncertainty, systematic investigation, advancement).
Link eligible work to claimable expenditures: 'To benefit from the incentives, you must link your eligible work to expenditures you can claim.'
File Form T661 (and T2SCH31 for corporations or T2038(IND) for individuals) with the income tax return.

documents_required.doc: Form T661 – Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) Expenditures Claim
Contemporaneous technical and financial documentation supporting the claim

eligibility.other_note: 'Corporations, individuals, trusts, and partnerships that conduct eligible work may be able to claim SR&ED tax incentives for the year.' The enhanced 35% refundable rate is limited to Canadian-controlled private corporations (CCPCs). Work must be conducted in Canada.

programmes.source_snippet: The Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) tax incentives are intended to encourage businesses to conduct research and development in Canada. ... There are 2 tax incentives: Claim a deduction against income; Earn an investment tax credit (ITC).

programmes.name_en: Strategic Response Fund (SRF, formerly Strategic Innovation Fund)
programmes.funder: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
programmes.amount_note: Large-scale contributions, historically for projects of at least CAD 20 million in eligible costs (CAD 10 million for some collaborative streams). Amounts are negotiated per project; no published cap.
programmes.deadline_note: Continuous intake via an online eligibility check followed by a consultation, plus periodic targeted calls for proposals (a food processing, supply chain and manufacturing call opened in June 2026).

procedure_steps.detail: Review the project requirements and the SRF key investment priorities (tariff response, innovation, AI Compute Challenge).
Complete the online eligibility check.
Request a consultation with the SRF team.
Submit a statement of interest, then a full application if invited; due diligence and negotiation of the contribution agreement.

eligibility.other_note: For-profit corporations incorporated in Canada; also open to not-for-profits and research institutions in collaborative streams. Aimed at large transformative projects, so early-stage startups are usually out of scope.

programmes.source_snippet: Building on the success of the former Strategic Innovation Fund (SIF), the SRF not only continues existing commitments but also expands support for industries affected by trade disruptions and tariff challenges.

programmes.amount_note: A suite of programs covering development, production, promotion and international marketing of Canadian feature films, plus the Talent to Watch programme for first features. Contribution amounts are set per stream and per project.
programmes.deadline_note: Streams operate on published annual or semi-annual deadlines set out in each program's guidelines.

eligibility.other_note: Canadian-controlled production companies; Canadian content requirements apply.

programmes.name_local: Fonds de prêts pour les femmes entrepreneures
programmes.funder: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED), delivered by non-profit lenders
programmes.amount_note: Loans of up to CAD 50,000 to women-owned and women-led businesses, delivered by selected non-profit delivery organisations rather than by ISED directly.
programmes.deadline_note: Availability depends on the individual delivery organisation; some partners periodically pause intake when their allocation is committed.
programmes.reopen_note: Where a delivery partner has paused, applicants are directed to another partner in the network; check the ISED partner list for organisations currently lending.

procedure_steps.detail: Find a delivery organisation serving your province or community.
Apply directly to that organisation.
Credit and business plan assessment.
Loan agreement and disbursement.

documents_required.doc: Proof that the business is at least 51% women-owned or women-led

eligibility.other_note: Business must be majority owned and led by women; delivery organisations set their own additional criteria.

programmes.funder: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
programmes.amount_note: Umbrella strategy delivering the Women Entrepreneurship Loan Fund (microloans up to CAD 50,000), the Ecosystem Fund supporting organisations that serve women entrepreneurs, and the Women Entrepreneurship Knowledge Hub.
programmes.deadline_note: The Loan Fund is delivered continuously by third-party lenders; Ecosystem Fund calls are periodic.

eligibility.other_note: Women-owned or women-led businesses in Canada. Loans are delivered through partner organisations rather than directly by the department.
